html:
The Bangladesh Liberation War of 1971 was the war in which East Pakistan broke away from Pakistan and became Bangladesh, with India's help.

Bengalis had resented rule from West Pakistan since the Bengali Language Movement of 1952, and the Bhola cyclone made it worse. When the army would not let Sheikh Mujibur Rahman take power after his 1970 election win, Yahya Khan ordered Operation Searchlight on the night of 25 March 1971. The army killed students, Hindus and nationalists in Dhaka and across the province; this became the Bangladesh genocide.

Bengali soldiers and volunteers formed the Mukti Bahini and fought a guerrilla war. About ten million people fled to India in the refugee crisis. In December, Indira Gandhi sent in the Indian army, and the Indo-Pakistani War lasted thirteen days. On 16 December the Pakistani forces in Dhaka surrendered, and about 93,000 soldiers became prisoners. Bangladesh was born.
sum: The Bangladesh Liberation War of 1971 was the war in which East Pakistan broke away from Pakistan and became Bangladesh, with India's help.
